items.what: 'Standing at a dock' is decided twice from ns.NearestDock's yards: Alert.lua:12/60 (120 yd) and Tracker.lua:201-203 (120 yd, 160 once shown). Canonical home: a single dock-radius constant (or predicate) beside ns.NearestDock in Core.lua.
items.why: Alert's dock alert is meant for the same situation the tracker shows the dock's departures for; if either radius changes, a player could get an arrival alert for a dock the tracker is not showing (or vice versa). The 160 yd hysteresis in Tracker is intentional and has no counterpart in Alert, so the shared fact is the 120 yd entry radius.
items.reason: Core.lua supplies both callbacks the same nearest-dock distance; a headless LuaJIT probe confirmed both accept 120 yards and reject 121 on entry, while Tracker alone retains a displayed dock through 160. Their different settings, ride precedence, nil handling and departure filtering do not require separate entry-radius values; sharing that constant preserves those differences.

items.what: The arrival fade (fully faded at 15 yd, opaque from 40 yd) is restated in Arrow.lua:49 and Route.lua:782 (the minimap line's fade near the goal).
items.why: Both fade guidance out as the player reaches the destination, and Arrow passes the result on to the native marker (`fading`). If the fade distances are tuned in one, the arrow/marker and the minimap line fade at different distances. A shared ns.ArrivalFade(distance) (or two named constants) would keep them together. Could be coincidental tuning, hence low.
items.reason: CHANGELOG.md:171–175 describes coordinated arrival fading, and a read-only LuaJIT probe confirmed identical Arrow/Route alpha values at 0, 15, 20, 27.5, 40 and 60 yards. Their activation conditions and display targets differ, but neither requires separate definitions of the 15–40-yard fade; sharing that calculation can preserve both contracts.

items.quote: local t = length > 0 and math.max(0, math.min(1, ((x - a.x) * dx + (y - a.y) * dy) / length)) or 0
items.what: Arrow re-implements walk progress: nearest-segment projection in ns.RefreshGuideStops (Arrow.lua:109-120) and the yards left along the path (Arrow.lua:64-68, recomputed every 0.05 s). Other copies: ns.OnWalk (Journey.lua:295-317, canonical; also used by Corpse.lua:101) and Tracker.lua JourneyDistance (Tracker.lua:129-148).
items.why: The listed anti-pattern 'walk progress in Arrow.lua, Tracker.lua and Journey's OnWalk' is still present. Differences: OnWalk rejects positions beyond ON_PATH (reach) and checks only a.map; Arrow has no reach limit and requires both a.map and b.map. OnWalk already returns `found` (segment index) and `after` (yards remaining), which is exactly what Arrow resumes from and displays. A change to how progress is measured (e.g. the off-path reach, map checks across loading-screen points) must be made in three places.
items.reason: These consumers require different contracts: Arrow follows retained bends or the guideStops endpoint, OnWalk measures projected progress for route reuse, and Tracker adds off-path distance and handles transport/loading-screen geometry. A read-only LuaJIT probe produced Arrow/OnWalk/Tracker distances of 151/150/162 yards at the same position, and 141/200/200 with guideStops enabled; OnWalk's results cannot directly replace the other calculations while preserving their behavior.

items.what: Core.lua mixes six responsibilities: settings defaults + SavedVariables bootstrap and module start (1-59, 312-340); server clock (61-71); the sighting store (73-110); world-point location and dock naming (112-178); nearest dock and departures timetable queries (180-310: NearestDock, RouteShown, KindShown, DockVisits, DockDepartures, ByDestination, NextStop); the shared travel ticker (342-400).

items.what: goalError's module-level lifetime is dead: it is only read in the two statements right after it is assigned inside RefreshCosts' consider (lines 288-291), so keeping it as a file upvalue and resetting it in Costs.Clear (line 474) is a dead store; it should be a local in consider (fully dead state, not a dead value)

No other file can reach a file-local upvalue: it is not exported through Costs, ns or Costs.Status (which returns costError, not goalError), so there is no dynamic dispatch, public surface, manifest, data-driven or cross-boundary path. Not persisted, not a SavedVariables key, not a test seam (no spec reads it). Every read follows a fresh assignment in the same call, so the value carried between calls and the Clear reset are never observed. items.what: bakedBound (JourneyCosts.lua:198-214) re-derives Planner's Walks.lua lookup: place keys as kind .. id (also JourneyCosts.lua:193 fixedPlace), the sorted "a b" pair key and the dry/water + reverse-slot index. Copies: Planner.lua:212-230 PlaceKey/BakedCost (canonical reader, but local so Journey cannot call it), tools/bake_walks.lua:29-43 and 96-98 (the writer, which also restates the place list of Planner.Places with its own "dock"/"taxi"/"portal"/"teleport" .. id keys and id*2-1/id*2 portal ends). Differences today: bakedBound returns 0 for first == last, swaps ends for a reverse batch and subtracts 0.5 for rounding (all intentional, caller-side); the key and slot arithmetic are identical, so no drift yet. bake_walks differs from Planner.Places intentionally (no faction or portal.requires filter, teleport.to rather than the flattened teleport point); planner_spec.lua:427-456 re-derives the keys too and catches a missing pair, which limits but does not remove the drift risk on the reader side.

The TOC loads Planner before JourneyCosts, and bake_walks.lua already loads Planner, so no import constraint forces duplicate decoding; the writer’s eligibility/landing differences and independent test fixtures do not refute the reader duplication.
